items.title: Dostaliśmy Fable 5.2! Przejrzałem dla Was niemal wszystkie materiały dostępne po starcie, wykonałem kilka ws†ępnych test
items.summary:
Dostaliśmy Fable 5.2! Przejrzałem dla Was niemal wszystkie materiały dostępne po starcie, wykonałem kilka ws†ępnych testów i poniżej moje wnioski.

1. Do długich, ambitnych projektów nie ma dziś lepszego modelu

Testerzy ze wcześniejszym dostępem opisują, że Fable 5.2 pokazuje, co potrafi, dopiero gdy dostanie odpowiednio ambitny projekt. Mowa o zadaniach, nad którymi model pracuje sam przez wiele godzin, czasem całą noc albo weekend.

Ethan Mollick, profesor Wharton, pisze o nierównym, ale jednak - AGI. 

Mollick poprosił Fable 5.2 o pracę naukową i dostał 182 strony. Merytorycznie było naprawdę dobrze - na poziomie doktoranta. Natomiast model niczego z niej nie wyciął (np: niepotrzebnego kontekstu), nie wyczyścił i nie uprościł, więc tekst nie nadawał się do publikacji.

W innym teście 28 zespołów agentów, czyli kopii modelu z osobnymi zadaniami, budowało razem trójwymiarowe, wyimaginowane światy. Wyszło naprawdę kreatywnie i ciekawie.

Natomiast bez pytania Ethana o opinię, samodzielnie podjęli decyzję o spisaniu sobie regulaminu, który po 12 dniach liczył 87,5 tys. słów - tyle co spora książka. 

Przez samodzielnie wdrożoną biurkrację, zamiast kilkuset światów dziennie zaczęło powstawać kilkanaście.

Niestety, wygląda na to, że cena, czy wynik jest za długi, nudny albo nie na temat, nadal należy do Ciebie. I to wydaje się problemem LLM-ów, którego jeszcze długo (nigdy?) nie uda się rozwiązać. A bez tego nie dostaniemy pełnej autonomii.

2. Poprawa możliwości jest nierówna: czipy i kod w górę, finanse i prawo w miejscu

GDPx to benchmark z SemiAnalysis, w którym zadania układają praktycy z konkretnych branż. Moim zdaniem jest to najlepszy test mierzący postęp w kierunku AGI, którą ja definiuję jako uniwersalnego współpracownika. 

Fable 5.2 zajął w nim pierwsze miejsce z wynikiem 16,4%. Opus 5.5 ma 12%, Astra 6 9.5%, Fable 5.1 8,5%.

Według SemiAnalysis model jest wyraźnie lepszy w projektowaniu czipów, tworzeniu oprogramowania, biologii i materiałoznawstwie. Nie jest lepszy w finansach, prawie, tradingu, projektowaniu sprzętu ani w RSI, czyli zadaniach, w których AI ulepsza samo siebie. Tu Anthropic celowo osłabił model, o czym sami wspominają w karcie systemowej.

W praktyce oznacza to tyle, że jeśli Twoja firma żyje z analiz finansowych albo umów, wejście w wyższe koszty związane z Fable 5.2 prawdopodobnie nie ma sensu.

3. Medium to może być rozsądny wybór, Max to pułapka

Fable 5.2 jest znacznie szybszy od Fable 5.1 i oszczędniej zużywa tokeny. W większości zadań kosztuje wyraźnie mniej niż poprzednik przy tych samych poziomach rozumowania. Również dzięki mniejszym o 20% kosztom per token.

W testach Artificial Analysis, Fable 5.2 przy medium kosztuje mniej więcej tyle, co Opus 5.5 przy high (około 14,90 zł wobec 13,50 zł za zadanie), a potrafi więcej. Jeżeli używasz Opusa high przez API, przetestuj Fable medium - możesz dostać lepsze wyniki za podobne pieniądze.

Powyżej robi się bardzo drogo. High to ponad 35 zł za zadanie, a Max już 104 zł, czyli siedem razy więcej niż medium. 

Max omijaj za wszelką cenę. Tak jak w poprzednich modelach Claude, ten poziom służy głównie do wyciskania budżetów korporacji, w których nikt nie odpowiada za koszty i podbijaniu marży Anthropic. W większości zadań absolkutnie nie wychodziłbym powyżej high.

4. W subskrypcji to nie jest model do codziennej pracy

Nie wiadomo jeszcze, jak niższy koszt zadania przełoży się na limity w abonamencie, zwłaszcza że Anthropic utrzymał absurdalne ograniczenie modeli Fable do 50% tygodniowego limitu. Na razie wygląda to słabo: Fable 5.2 zjada limit planu za około 390 zł / mies w błyskawicznym tempie i do codziennej pracy się nie nadaje.

W normalnej pracy, limit 5h wyczerpałem bez szczególnych starań w mniej niż godzinę.

5. Obsługa komputera nadal słabsza niż w tanich modelach GPT

Wykonałem kilka testów i Fable 5.2 wciąż obsługuje komputer wyraźnie gorzej i wolniej niż modele GPT - nawet nieporównywalnie tańszy GPT 6.1 Terra. 

Jeśli AI ma za Ciebie regularnie wykonywać zadania w przeglądarce - odpuść Fable i zostań przy modelach GPT. Przynajmniej jako subagencie.

6. Na co dzień zostaję przy Opusie

Na ten moment dodaję Fable 5.2 high jako recenzenta planów i wykonawcę absolutnie najtrudniejszych zadań / analiz. W 95% codziennej pracy zostaję przy Opusie 5.5 high/xhigh, bo wzrost możliwości nie uzasadnia wyższych kosztów, szczególnie w subskrypcji.

Pełna recenzja jak zawsze za +/- 2 tygodnie, oraz na naszej stronie w zakładce "Jaki model AI do pracy?". Obserwuj mój profil, żeby tego nie przegapić.

Testowałeś już Fable 5.2? Jakie są Twoje wstępne wnioski?

items.title: When your imaginary best friend becomes part of your photoshoot.🥹
items.summary:
When your imaginary best friend becomes part of your photoshoot.🥹

Made with GPT image 2.6 flare 

Prompt: Create an ultra-realistic, premium mixed-media fashion editorial photograph featuring a beautiful young East Asian woman lying playfully on her stomach, combined with a charming hand-drawn black-and-white pencil-sketch cartoon character. The artwork should seamlessly blend high-end professional studio photography with traditional graphite illustration, creating a whimsical, playful, aesthetically pleasing editorial composition.

1. SUBJECT — WOMAN'S APPEARANCE

A beautiful young adult East Asian woman with:
Long, voluminous, naturally wavy dark-brown hair.
Soft, wispy curtain bangs framing her forehead.
Fair, naturally glowing skin with realistic texture.
Delicate facial features and natural makeup.
Soft rosy cheeks and glossy pink lips.
A playful facial expression with one eye closed in a wink and lips gently puckered.
White wireless earbuds.
A delicate silver necklace with a small cross pendant.

Her appearance should feel youthful, natural, elegant, and effortlessly photogenic.

2. POSE & BODY POSITION

The woman is lying comfortably on her stomach on a smooth studio floor.

Her upper body is slightly elevated.
Her head is tilted gently toward the camera.
One hand supports the side of her face near her ear.
Her other arm extends naturally forward along the floor.
Her legs are bent upward at the knees, with both feet lifted behind her.
Her white sneakers and soles are partially visible in the upper-left area.
Her body is positioned diagonally across the frame.
Her face is turned toward the camera, creating an intimate, playful connection with the viewer.

The pose should look relaxed, spontaneous, feminine, and editorial rather than overly staged.

3. OUTFIT & ACCESSORIES

Preserve the following outfit:

Top:
A loose-fitting, off-white blouse featuring tiny scattered blue floral motifs, a delicate textured fabric, long puff sleeves, elasticated cuffs, and a relaxed feminine silhouette.
Bottom:
Light-wash blue denim jeans with a relaxed fit and visible denim texture.

Footwear:
Clean white casual sneakers with white soles and matching white socks.
The outfit should have realistic fabric folds, natural wrinkles, and detailed stitching.

4. CARTOON CHARACTER — JERRY
Position a charming Jerry-style cartoon mouse directly on the woman's lower-back and belly area.

The mouse should be rendered entirely in traditional black-and-white graphite pencil illustration.

Character details:

Large expressive rounded ears.

Small oval nose.

Prominent expressive eyes.
Fine whiskers.
Wide cheerful smile with an open mouth.
Detailed pencil-shaded fur.
Small arms and legs.
A thin curved mouse tail extending naturally behind him.
Character pose:
The mouse is lying comfortably on the woman's back, with his elbows resting on her blouse and both hands supporting his chin. He looks delighted and fascinated, gazing toward the woman's face.
Add two small hand-drawn heart doodles and a few expressive motion marks above his head.

The cartoon must appear physically integrated into the photograph, with convincing placement and subtle contact shadows.

5. ARTISTIC STYLE & MIXED-MEDIA TREATMENT

The most important visual characteristic is the contrast between two artistic mediums:

Woman: 100% photorealistic professional fashion photography, realistic skin, detailed hair strands, natural lighting, authentic fabric textures.

Cartoon: Traditional monochrome graphite pencil sketch, visible pencil strokes, cross-hatching, hand-drawn outlines, textured shading, expressive facial features.

Do not make the woman look illustrated or animated. Keep the cartoon entirely in its original hand-drawn pencil-sketch appearance.

The combination should look like an artist has physically drawn a cartoon character into a real studio photograph.

6. BACKGROUND & ENVIRONMENT

Minimalist seamless light-gray studio background.

Matching light-gray studio floor.

Soft natural-looking shadows beneath the woman.

No furniture, unnecessary objects, or distracting decorations.
Clean, spacious editorial composition.
7. LIGHTING & CAMERA
Professional softbox studio lighting.
Soft, diffused illumination from the front.

Gentle shadows around the subject.

Natural skin highlights.
Balanced exposure.
Sharp focus on the woman's face and cartoon character.
Professional fashion editorial photography.
Slightly elevated three-quarter camera perspective.
Full-body horizontal lying pose captured within a vertical frame.
8. COMPOSITION & OUTPUT
Aspect ratio: 3:4 vertical portrait.
High-resolution image.

Subject positioned predominantly on the right side.

Cartoon character positioned on the left-center, resting on the woman's back.
Both the woman's face and cartoon character must remain clearly visible.
Preserve the complete playful interaction.
Balanced negative space around the subjects.
9. NEGATIVE PROMPT
Avoid distorted anatomy, extra fingers, malformed hands, unnatural body proportions, floating cartoon characters, incorrect contact shadows, blurry faces, plastic-looking skin, excessive beauty filters, cartoon-style human skin, colored cartoon illustrations, 3D-rendered characters, messy backgrounds, excessive doodles, unwanted accessories, incorrect clothing, and cropped facial features.
FINAL VISUAL GOAL: An exceptionally realistic mixed-media fashion photograph where a real young woman poses playfully with a charming graphite pencil-sketch cartoon mouse resting on her back. The final result should feel like a professional creative campaign combining photography, fashion, illustration, and playful storytelling.

items.title: Accurate medical advice from AI can still be dangerous | STAT
items.summary: Some will argue that AI should be a neutral aggregator of information. But AI cannot be neutral: Every accurate answer excludes many additional facts and emphasizes some over others. Because of these choices, AI answers already influence behavior, as shown by the chickenpox party examples. [...] Artificial intelligence is delivering health guidance at an unprecedented scale. Every week, more than 300 million people ask ChatGPT health questions. Now, the federal government is moving AI deeper into medical care to communicate directly and autonomously with patients. Chris Klomp, the nominee for deputy secretary of Health and Human Services, has called AI in patient care the agency’s “holy grail” for improving the nation’s health. [...] Medical ethics pairs the duty to do no harm with beneficence, which is an affirmative obligation to do good. Safety evaluations of AI have focused mainly on the first duty by screening for responses that encourage imminent self-harm, discourage necessary care, or spread false information. Behavioral benchmarking would extend the first duty beyond imminent danger to long-term harms. It could also advance the second duty, which has received far less attention: designing AI to help people by

items.title: Why is Nvidia so powerful in the AI world, and what could Jensen Huang’s scandal really cost?
items.summary:
The AI sector is notorious for the amount of circular financing going on – where companies invest in their own suppliers or customers. Nvidia is a key player in this loop.

Investors are already fretting over whether the enormous amounts of money sunk into AI can ever return profits.

While leading AI model builders Anthropic and OpenAI are moving toward public listings or fresh funding rounds, both face harsh reality checks. [...] The now multi-trillion-dollar company got its start making chips called graphic processing units (GPUs), used largely for video games. However, these chips – and their successors – turned out to be ideal for the kind of number-crunching needed for training and using AI models.

Other companies such as Google and AMD have tried to make chips that can compete with Nvidia for speed and efficiency, however neither has been able to displace Nvidia from its dominance of the AI market. [...] Computer chips – specifically the chips used to produce and run artificial intelligence (AI) systems – have become a key front in the United States’ rivalry with China for geopolitical power and influence. The most powerful chips are needed for the most advanced AI, and the US has tried to maintain its edge over China by restricting access to those chips.

While the Chinese government rejects claims of espionage, Alice Huang has reportedly been under investigation by the US for years.

items.summary: Theo hướng dẫn, các giải pháp được xem xét công nhận là sáng kiến bao gồm: giải pháp kỹ thuật, giải pháp quản lý, giải pháp tác nghiệp và giải pháp ứng dụng tiến bộ kỹ thuật. Trong đó, giải pháp kỹ thuật có thể là sản phẩm, vật liệu, giống cy trồng, vật nuôi hoặc quy trình công nghệ; giải pháp quản lý là phương pháp tổ chức, điều hành công việc; giải pháp tác nghiệp là các phương pháp thực hiện nghiệp vụ chuyên môn; còn giải pháp ứng dụng tiến bộ kỹ thuật là việc áp dụng các giải pháp kỹ thuật [...] Đối với các đề tài khoa học, đề án khoa học và công trình khoa học – công nghệ, việc xét nghiệm thu thực hiện theo quy định của pháp luật về khoa học và công nghệ. Các đề tài chỉ được xem xét công nhận hiệu quả áp dụng và phạm vi ảnh hưởng khi đã được nghiệm thu đạt yêu cầu trở lên. [...] giải pháp kỹ thuật đã có vào thực tiễn.

items.title: Định hướng thúc đẩy ngoại giao khoa học và công nghệ

items.title: Elon Musk: 'Công nghệ Neuralink có thể chữa mù' - Báo VnExpress
items.summary: Theo Tom's Hardware, Blindsight khác với đa số công nghệ hiện nay, vốn tập trung vào truyền tín hiệu từ não bộ để điều khiển thiết bị bên ngoài. Ví dụ, ốc tai điện tử và thiết bị cấy ghép thần kinh cảm giác gửi tín hiệu từ cảm biến vào não, giúp người khiếm thính nghe lại và bệnh nhn lấy lại xúc giác. Trong khi đó, Blindsight hướng đến thiết lập đường dẫn thị giác nhn tạo, cho phép bệnh nhn dùng camera để thu thập hình ảnh, sau đó chuyển đổi tín hiệu thành dạng mà não bộ hiểu được thông qua [...] Dù không phải công ty đầu tiên nghiên cứu về giao diện não - máy tính, Neuralink là một trong những tên tuổi thành công nhất, phần nào nhờ hỗ trợ tài chính từ Musk. Một số doanh nghiệp khác cũng nỗ lực nghiên cứu công nghệ tương tự. Ví dụ, Meta phát triển máy quét điện não đồ từ trường không xm lấn cho phép người dùng chuyển suy nghĩ thành những thao tác nhấn phím, trong khi startup Trung Quốc NeuroXess, thành lập năm 2021, đang đẩy nhanh tiến độ để thử nghiệm trên người trong năm nay. [...] Neuralink đã tiến hành một số thử nghiệm công nghệ cho người bị tổn thương tủy sống, bệnh xơ cứng teo cơ một bên (ALS) và bệnh lý khác. Vài năm gần đy, công ty cũng công bố một số ca cấy ghép não. Hồi tháng 1, Neuralink cho biết có 21 người đã tham gia thử nghiệm trên toàn thế giới.

items.title: Accurate medical advice from AI can still be dangerous | STAT
items.summary: Some will argue that AI should be a neutral aggregator of information. But AI cannot be neutral: Every accurate answer excludes many additional facts and emphasizes some over others. Because of these choices, AI answers already influence behavior, as shown by the chickenpox party examples. [...] Artificial intelligence is delivering health guidance at an unprecedented scale. Every week, more than 300 million people ask ChatGPT health questions. Now, the federal government is moving AI deeper into medical care to communicate directly and autonomously with patients. Chris Klomp, the nominee for deputy secretary of Health and Human Services, has called AI in patient care the agency’s “holy grail” for improving the nation’s health. [...] Medical ethics pairs the duty to do no harm with beneficence, which is an affirmative obligation to do good. Safety evaluations of AI have focused mainly on the first duty by screening for responses that encourage imminent self-harm, discourage necessary care, or spread false information. Behavioral benchmarking would extend the first duty beyond imminent danger to long-term harms. It could also advance the second duty, which has received far less attention: designing AI to help people by

items.title: Why is Nvidia so powerful in the AI world, and what could Jensen Huang’s scandal really cost?
items.summary:
The AI sector is notorious for the amount of circular financing going on – where companies invest in their own suppliers or customers. Nvidia is a key player in this loop.

Investors are already fretting over whether the enormous amounts of money sunk into AI can ever return profits.

While leading AI model builders Anthropic and OpenAI are moving toward public listings or fresh funding rounds, both face harsh reality checks. [...] The now multi-trillion-dollar company got its start making chips called graphic processing units (GPUs), used largely for video games. However, these chips – and their successors – turned out to be ideal for the kind of number-crunching needed for training and using AI models.

Other companies such as Google and AMD have tried to make chips that can compete with Nvidia for speed and efficiency, however neither has been able to displace Nvidia from its dominance of the AI market. [...] Computer chips – specifically the chips used to produce and run artificial intelligence (AI) systems – have become a key front in the United States’ rivalry with China for geopolitical power and influence. The most powerful chips are needed for the most advanced AI, and the US has tried to maintain its edge over China by restricting access to those chips.

While the Chinese government rejects claims of espionage, Alice Huang has reportedly been under investigation by the US for years.

items.title: Recent advances in AI are creating a 'paradigm shift' for robotics - Berkeley News
items.summary:
Traditionally, engineers can directly program the software that tells robots how to perceive objects, plan movements and control their actions, a process called model-based robotics. Or, with model-free robotics, they can train robots to learn behaviors from demonstrations through imitation learning. The first approach requires extensive engineering, while the second needs enormous amounts of data and time. [...] Berkeley-based Ambi Robotics, which specializes in logistics and warehouse order fulfillment, applied the new methods earlier this year to analyze parcel sorting data and test updates to robot behavior. Tests showed an increased capacity of over 15,000 packages sorted annually per robot; the change is now deployed across 30% of the company’s U.S. fleet. [...] Ken Goldberg

“Agentic robotics is a fundamental shift in how robots are controlled,” Goldberg said. “Instead of collecting massive amounts of data and hand-tuning every behavior, teams of agents can quickly generate, test and refine robot programs that allow human engineers to interpret how the programs work for fine-tuning and verification.”

items.title: AI² Robotics Joins Indonesia’s National Strategic Industries | Gasgoo
items.summary:
Underpinning this deployment is AI² Robotics's integrated "Model × Hardware × Scenario" capability. The approach centers on a brain-like embodied large model as the intelligence core, mass-producible and stable robotic bodies as the vehicle, and real-world productivity scenarios as the driving force. [...] Gasgoo Munich-On November 9, AI² Robotics announced it has signed a memorandum of understanding with the Danantara Development Management Fund (DDMF), the investment arm of Indonesia's state-backed wealth fund Danantara Indonesia. The partnership will focus on pilot applications, industrial collaboration, and local deployment of general-purpose intelligent robots and embodied AI technology across the archipelago. [...] The agreement was signed during the inaugural Danantara Technology Innovation Investment Forum (DTIIF 2026) in Jakarta, with Zhang Peng, AI² Robotics's co-founder, signing on behalf of the company.

Image Credit: AI² Robotics

Operating independently under the president's office, Danantara Indonesia holds substantial influence. AI² Robotics is now the first—and currently the only—robotics company to join DDMF's embodied AI cooperation roster.

items.title: Geek+ Unveils 24/7 Warehouse Autonomy Plan to Advance Self-Optimizing, Around-the-Clock Operation | Morningstar
items.summary: Geek+ offers a comprehensive portfolio of end-to-end warehouse robotics solutions, spanning tote-, pallet- and shelf-based workflows and applications such as material transport, storage, retrieval and order picking. Its AMR systems support high-throughput execution of structured tasks, while embodied AI is being developed to extend automation into more variable handling activities and exception recovery. Together, these capabilities form an important foundation for continuous autonomous [...] Physical AI is extending robotics beyond highly structured material-handling tasks into more complex manipulation and exception handling. Meanwhile, advances in AI are bringing greater intelligence to robot fleet coordination, warehouse workflows and day-to-day operations. Together, these developments are laying the groundwork for a new operating model: autonomous warehousing. [...] "Over the past 11 years, Geek+ has demonstrated that warehouse robotics can deliver value at scale in real operations around the world," said Yong Zheng, Founder and CEO of Geek+. "Our next goal is to enable the warehouse as a whole to operate more autonomously and continuously improve. By advancing embodied AI and warehouse-wide intelligence-and building on our global deployment capabilities-we aim to make autonomous warehouses a practical foundation for the next generation of logistics."

items.title: Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20
items.summary:
Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.

items.title: OpenAI kicks off charm offensive to change voters' view of data centers | Reuters

SAN FRANCISCO, Nov 5 (Reuters) - Stunning ​victories by Democrats in US midterm elections this week have been interpreted by many as Americans repudiating tech ‌industry plans to build data centers across the country. OpenAI has now embarked on new strategies to change their minds.

The AI lab on Thursday laid out policies — in the works since August — intended to help the company build more trust with local communities and convince them that data centers will ​benefit them. [...] OpenAI officials, along with many of their peers in tech, ​have spent the last ⁠two years trying to build ties with the administration of US President Donald Trump in hopes of shaping federal policy around AI.

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman donated $1 million to Trump's inaugural committee and later attended Trump's second inauguration. Last year, Brockman donated $25 million in his personal capacity to ⁠a Trump ​super PAC. [...] The Reuters Daily Briefing newsletter provides all the news you need to start your day. Sign up here.

items.title: OpenAI employees warned about operational security lapses for years, sources say | Reuters
items.summary:
OpenAI and Anthropic have tried to ​maintain a more open research culture to both ⁠attract employees and foster creativity that can lead to breakthroughs. The AI field is rooted in academia, where machine-learning scientists have openly discussed their research.

Some OpenAI employees are increasingly worried about this approach as AI grows more capable, according to the five people. [...] When asked about employees' concerns and their view that management did not act on these issues, OpenAI spokesperson Elana Widmann ​said that OpenAI is one of the most targeted organizations in the world. As a result, the company invests heavily in its security program to protect against attacks from insiders, cybercriminals and nation-states, she said. [...] The Reuters Daily Briefing newsletter provides all the news you need to start your day. Sign up here.

These workers argued that OpenAI's controls were so lax ‌that outsiders, including foreign governments, could obtain sensitive information about the AI lab's technology with relative ease, the people said. For example, anybody at OpenAI who could access its code could see the technical details underlying many company projects.
